chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

I said to him (peace be upon him): A man dies and upon him is five hundred dirhams of Zakat, and upon him is the Hajj of Islam, and he leaves three hundred dirhams. So he bequeaths with the Hajj of Islam, and that the debt of Zakat be fulfilled from him. He (peace be upon him) said: Hajj is performed on his behalf from the nearest [portion], and the remainder is given for the Zakat.

key_terms.حَجَّةُ الْإِسْلَامِ: The Hajj of Islam (the obligatory pilgrimage)
key_terms.يُحَجُّ عَنْهُ: Hajj is performed on his behalf

ai.seo_question: How are Zakat and Hajj debts prioritized when a deceased person's estate is insufficient to pay both?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the distribution of a deceased's estate when funds are insufficient to cover both the obligatory Hajj and Zakat debts. It establishes that the Hajj is fulfilled first using the exact amount required for the ritual, while the remaining balance is allocated to settle the Zakat debt, reflecting the Shia juristic view of prioritizing the core pillar of Hajj over the financial obligation of Zakat in cases of scarcity. This ruling underscores the principle that religious duties are discharged proportionally from the estate based on their specific financial requirements.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,

‘I said to himasws, ‘A man is dying and upon him is five hundred Dirhams of Zakāt, and upon him is the (performance) of Hajj of Al-Islam, and leaves three hundred Dirhams. So he bequeaths with (the performance of) the Hajj of Al-Islam, and that the debt of Zakāt to be fulfilled from him’. Heasws said: ‘Hajj would be performed on his behalf from the nearest of what can happen to be, and the remainder would be extracted regarding the Zakāt’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “

I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who at death owed five hundred dirham of Zakat and one Hajjatu al-Islam. His legacy is three hundred dirham. He has made a will about performing Hajjatu al-Islam for him as well as to pay his debt of Zakat. He (the Imam) said, ‘Hajj must be performed for him from the closest distance (Makkah) and the rest is paid for his Zakat.’”
